newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli businessmen to meet Arafat soon. [CORRECTED 12:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israeli businessmen to meet Arafat soon. [CORRECTED 12:45 GMT]

text.p: A group of top Israeli businessmen plans to meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Gaza in mid-September to discuss ways to advance economic ties.
The delegation will be led by Benjamin Gaon, president and chief executive of Koor Industries Ltd, Israel's largest holding concern. (Corrects Gaon's position from chairman and chief executive).

"We the business leaders cannot sit on the side and criticise all the time and say how bad the situation is. We have to get involved and the meeting with Arafat demonstrates our commitment to the peace process and to cementing our relations with the Palestinians," Gaon told Reuters.

The group will include the chairmen of Israel's leading banks, the president and chief executive of Clal Israel Ltd David Wainshal, Israel Borovich, head of Arkia Israeli Airlines Ltd, and Michael Strauss, head of Nahariya Dairy Strauss Ltd.
The two sides will discuss the closure which bars many Palestinians from working in Israel, creating economic hardships in self-ruled Gaza and the West Bank.
The closure was imposed in the aftermath of a series of suicide bombings by Moslem militants in February and March and has been eased somewhat.

Gaon said the meeting was not a political statement but added: "If we want to continue with the peace process, businessmen have to be concerned about the economic situation of residents of the Palestinian territories."
Gaon's spokesman said the meeting was organised with the approval of Israel's Foreign Ministry.

Gaon, who openly supported the reelection campaign of Labour leader Shimon Peres, recently expressed concern about how the closure would affect the Palestinians and said it could be an obstacle to peace.

Peres was defeated by hardline Likud leader Benjamin Netanyahu, who has yet to meet Arafat. Three days of talks have failed to fix a summit between the Israeli and Palestinian leaders, seen as vital for reviving their stalled self-rule agreement for the West Bank and Gaza.
